scenarios.title: Local synthetic team membership lifecycle
plannedActions: POST /v1/teams with padded synthetic name
GET created team as owner
POST member invitation as owner
POST member invitation join while team is free
GET team after rejected free-plan join
Fixture only: seed active entitlement in owned D1
POST valid member invitation after fixture entitlement
POST same invitation again as existing member
GET team after duplicate member join
POST viewer invitation as owner
POST viewer invitation as viewer actor
POST viewer invitation as existing member
GET team as nonmanager member
POST invitation as nonmanager member
PATCH team name as nonmanager member
DELETE owner membership as owner
PATCH member role to admin as owner
GET team as newly appointed admin
PATCH team name as admin
GET viewer team list after rename
PATCH viewer to admin as admin
PATCH owner role as admin
POST team project as admin
GET project as viewer
PATCH viewer to member as admin
GET project after viewer promotion
DELETE project as ordinary member
DELETE own membership as ordinary member
GET own identity after leaving team
GET project after leaving team
DELETE viewer invitation as admin
GET team invitation list after revocation
POST revoked invitation as outsider
GET outsider identity after revoked join
DELETE admin membership as owner
GET team after owner removed admin
GET team as removed admin
DELETE team project as owner
GET owner project list after archive
GET archived project as owner
expectedOutcomes: Creation returns trimmed name, free plan and authenticated owner role.
Readback contains exactly the owner membership and no invitations.
Owner creates a member invitation with exact one-day lifetime and local URL.
A valid invitation cannot admit a member while the team is free.
Rejected free-plan join leaves only the owner membership.
Synthetic fixture setup updates exactly one owned team; no payment or subscription transition is asserted.
Entitled team admits a member through its valid invitation.
A sequential duplicate join returns the existing member role.
Duplicate join creates no second membership in public readback.
Owner creates a viewer invitation with default 30-day lifetime.
Viewer invitation admits the requested viewer role.
An existing member joining a viewer invitation retains its member role.
Nonmanager member sees membership list but no invitation management rows.
A nonmanager cannot create invitations.
A member cannot rename the team.
The owner cannot remove its own membership.
Owner can promote a member to admin.
Promoted admin reads its persisted role, both invitations, and the unchanged original Synthetic team name after the denied member rename.
Admin can rename the team with whitespace trimmed.
Viewer team list reflects the admin rename and unchanged viewer membership.
An admin cannot appoint another admin.
An admin cannot change the owner membership.
Admin creates a team project owned by the team owner.
Viewer project readback explicitly reports read-only access.
Admin can promote a viewer to ordinary member.
After promotion public project readback changes to member and writable.
A writable ordinary member cannot archive the project.
A nonowner ordinary member can leave the team.
Self-leave removes the team and project from public identity lists.
Departed member cannot read the former team project.
Admin can revoke the viewer invitation.
Public manager readback marks only the selected invitation revoked.
A revoked invitation cannot admit a new outsider.
Rejected revoked invitation leaves outsider without team or project access.
Owner can remove an admin membership.
Owner readback contains only the owner after self-leave and admin removal.
Removed admin cannot read the team.
Owner archives the team project.
Archived project disappears from owner project list.
Even its owner cannot retrieve an archived project via normal project read.
